findings.title: If Apple sends you a push notification alerting you to a spyware attack, take it seriously
findings.summary_md: Apple sent threat notifications on August 13, 2026 to users targeted in 110 countries, and said it has notified customers in over 150 countries to date. The notifications warn of mercenary spyware attacks and now arrive as a push alert on the iPhone lock screen, with email and account-login copies as well. Citizen Lab senior researcher John Scott-Railton first highlighted the latest batch in a thread on X. Apple says it does not attribute attacks to specific governments and cannot confirm whether a device was actually compromised.

findings.title: Heads-up: New round of Apple Threat Notifications is going out right now
findings.summary_md: Security researcher Costin Raiu posted the text of Apple's new threat notification, stating it was being sent to targeted users in 99 countries and that Apple had now notified users in over 150 countries in total. He noted the October round was distinct from the August wave and tied to new attacks rather than a retrospective review. Apple had not issued a public statement about the wave at the time of the post.

findings.title: Apple Sends New Threat Notifications to Users in 99 Countries
findings.summary_md: Apple began sending a new round of threat notifications on Friday, October 30, 2026 to targeted iPhone users in 99 countries, the second wave in eleven weeks. The 99-country figure and the over-150 total come from the notification text posted by Costin Raiu, not from a company announcement. Apple has never disclosed how many people receive the alerts and does not attribute them to specific attackers or regions. Genuine Apple threat notifications never ask recipients to click a link, open a file, install an app or profile, or provide a password or verification code.
